extracted.intended_audience: prospective PhD applicants and university nominators/administrators for the Google PhD Fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for university-nominated PhD students applying to the Google PhD Fellowship program, including eligibility, required materials, regional variations, research focus areas, and how proposals are reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are evaluated on the strength of the research proposal, research impact, student academic achievements, and leadership potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Canada and the United States, East Asia and Latin America, essay responses are evaluated in addition to application materials to determine an overall recommendation. A nominee's status as a member of a historically marginalized group is not considered in the selection of award recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal evaluation (novelty, robustness, impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research proposals are evaluated for innovative concepts that are relevant to Google’s research areas, as well as aspects of robustness and potential impact to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should include the direction and any plans of where your work is going in addition to a comprehensive description of the research you are pursuing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment to Google research areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should be relevant to Google's listed research areas (e.g., Computer Architecture, Algorithms and Optimization, Health Research, HCI, Machine Learning and ML Foundations, Machine Perception, NLP, Privacy/Safety/Security, Quantum Computing, Software Engineering & PL, Systems/Networking/Cloud).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics outside of these areas will still be considered, but applicants are encouraged to align their proposals with one of the listed areas. Region-specific research areas may also be listed in application forms during the application window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research alignment to Google AI Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should align with Google AI Principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are explicitly reminded that their research should align with Google's AI Principles; no further elaboration is provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student eligibility — enrollment and conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must remain enrolled full-time in the PhD program for the duration of the Fellowship or forfeit the award. Google employees and their spouses, children, and household members are not eligible. Students already supported by a comparable industry award are not eligible (government or non-profit funding is exempt). Past awardees are not eligible to apply again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of the Fellowship does not guarantee admission to a PhD program for incoming/early-stage nominees; awardees must separately be accepted to a PhD program where required (region-dependent).

rubrics_metrics.name: University eligibility for nomination
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities must be an accredited research institution that awards research degrees to PhD students in computer science (or an adjacent field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All award payments and recipients will be reviewed for compliance with relevant US and international laws, regulations and policies; Google reserves the right to withhold funding that may violate laws, regulations or policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination and submission process
rubrics_metrics.description: All students must be nominated for the fellowship by their university; applications must be submitted by an official representative of the university during the application window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities should contact their department or graduate school for information about internal nomination processes. Application submission portal will be available on the program page when the application period begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination limits per university
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on how many students each university may nominate vary by region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canada and the United States: up to four eligible students. Africa, Australia, New Zealand, East Asia, Europe, India, Southeast Asia and the Middle East: up to three eligible students. Latin America: universities may nominate any number of eligible students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required materials (all nominated students)
rubrics_metrics.description: Universities will need to submit the following materials in a single, flat (not portfolio) PDF file: Student CV with links to website and publications (if available); Research/dissertation proposal (maximum 3 pages, excluding references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All application materials should be submitted in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-specific required materials — Canada, United States, East Asia, Latin America
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional materials required in these regions include: Cover sheet signed by the Department Chair confirming the student passes eligibility requirements; Short (1-page) CV of the student's primary PhD advisor; 2-3 letters of recommendation (at least one from the thesis advisor for current PhD students); Transcripts of current and previous academic records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Canada, East Asia, and the United States also require student essay responses (350-word limit) to specified prompts on research impact and leadership (see separate rubric entry). For Latin America, specific essay prompts and a 3-page research proposal requirement are listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-specific required materials — Africa, Europe, and the Middle East
rubrics_metrics.description: Required items: Cover sheet signed by the Department Chair confirming the student passes eligibility requirements; Short (1-page) CV of the student's primary PhD advisor; 2-3 letters of recommendation from those familiar with the nominee's work (at least one from the thesis advisor for current PhD students); Transcripts of current and previous academic records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These materials are to be submitted together in the single PDF by the university nominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-specific required materials — Australia and New Zealand
rubrics_metrics.description: Required items: Transcripts of current and previous academic records; 1-2 letters of recommendation from those familiar with the nominee's work (at least one from the thesis advisor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early-stage students enrolled in the first or second year of their PhD are eligible (no requirement for completion of graduate coursework by the academic award year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-specific required materials — India and Southeast Asia
rubrics_metrics.description: Required items: Short (one-page) resume/CV of the student applicant's primary PhD program advisor; Available transcripts (mark sheets) starting from the first year/semester of Bachelor's degree to date; 2-3 letters of recommendation (at least one from the thesis advisor for current PhD students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For India, there are separate provisions for early-stage (up to 4-year fellowship contingent on registering full-time) and late-stage PhD students (1-year fellowship to recognize contributions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Region-specific required materials — Latin America (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required items for Latin America: Cover sheet signed by an official representative of the university confirming eligibility; Short (one-page) resume/CV of the student's primary PhD program advisor; Transcripts (mark sheets) starting from the first year/semester of Bachelor's degree to date; Research proposal (maximum 3 pages, excluding references); 2-3 letters of recommendation (at least one from the thesis advisor); Student essay responses (350-word limits) to specified prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Latin America nominations follow the region's specific prompts, including essays about research impact and long-term goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student essay prompts and word limits (where required)
rubrics_metrics.description: In specified regions (Canada/US, East Asia, Latin America) students must submit short essay responses (350-word limit) to prompts such as: describe the desired impact your research will make on the field and society and why this is important to you; describe an example of leadership experience; and for Latin America, an additional prompt on long-term goals and how the fellowship would help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essays are evaluated in addition to application materials to determine an overall recommendation in those regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research stage eligibility by region
rubrics_metrics.description: Region-dependent rules define which stages of PhD study are eligible: Africa/India/Latin America/Southeast Asia allow incoming or early-stage nominees (with conditions); Australia/NZ early-stage students in first or second year are eligible; Canada/US require students who have completed graduate coursework in their PhD by the academic award year; East Asia expects students who have completed most graduate coursework and have sufficient time for research after receiving the fellowship; Europe and the Middle East accept students enrolled at any stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For incoming/early-stage nominees, the fellowship award may be contingent on registering for a full-time PhD program in the award year; grant of fellowship does not equate to admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and completeness requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted in a single, flat (not portfolio) PDF file and all application materials should be in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete proposals will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative/award disbursement and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any monetary awards will be paid directly to the Fellow's university for distribution and no overhead should be assessed against them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship recipients are not subject to intellectual property restrictions unless they complete an internship at Google; in that case they are subject to the same IP restrictions as any other Google intern. Fellowship recipients do not become Google employees by virtue of the award.
